answer: To secure our network, each entity anchors its identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Rather than letting rogue nodes treat the network as an isolated island or an easy haven, registration enforces exponential capital exhaustion: every additional identity bonded by an operator costs exponentially more stake ($O(2^n)$). A velvet glove mechanism silently taxes unverified Sybil swarms, guaranteeing superlinear attacker cost.
